OWNED FILES (edit only these): tests/test_incident_engine.py, tests/test_incident_pressure.py (new), files under tests/fixtures/stories/lighthouse-incident/, and ONLY IF A TEST PROVES A REAL DEFECT: storygame/runtime/engine.py and storygame/runtime/incidents.py. Do NOT touch data/ or any other test. The runtime must never name 1C, the freight terminal or any story-specific id.

BACKGROUND (read first, read-only): .plans/game-reimagination-phase1.md (Step 1, 2, 3 results and section 3 step 4), .plans/1c-contract-result.md sections 'Missed window' and 'Completion, pressure, and successor', storygame/runtime/engine.py (_turn_active ~460-520, _activate_pacing ~1032, _prepare_handoff, _unresolved_incident), tests/test_incident_engine.py, tests/test_incident_characterization.py (rejection test), and the fixture tests/fixtures/stories/lighthouse-incident. Steps 1-3 are done: the engine resolves incident outcomes, completes the scene without the min_turns floor, and in an unresolved incident scene skips the resolution deadline backstop and drops outcome-advantage deliveries. The incident's pressure event is its missed_window_event_id (a pacing event); it fires from _activate_pacing on the commit path only.

GOAL (step 4): pin and, only if a test fails for a real reason, fix these contract rules on the lighthouse fixture:
(1) Rejection does not advance the pressure event: a turn whose proposal is rejected (see the characterization test for how to make the stub provider's narration get rejected) leaves turn_index, fired_event_ids, facts and active_event_ids unchanged; the pressure event (tide_turns, at_turn 2) does not fire; the next accepted turn that reaches turns_since_entry 2 fires it. Retrying the same rejected input twice still does not fire it.
(2) Clarification does not advance it: if a ClarificationTurn / EngineRefusalTurn can be produced from the stub provider in under 40 lines, assert the same unchanged state. If not, add a test for the closest engine-level path and say in the notes exactly what could not be reached.
(3) The missed window grants nothing: after tide_turns fires with no outcome, no outcome advantage fact (chart_copied, boat_route_known) and no outcome cost (chart_page_torn) is true, tide_has_turned is true, scene is still 1A, and it stays 1A through several more accepted no-op turns past handoff_after_turns (3), including turn 6. The event fires exactly once (fired_event_ids) and its fact is not re-asserted or duplicated.
(4) Late recovery works: after the missed window has fired, the player earns outcome copy_chart (or learn_route) on a later turn; the outcome facts and its own cost assert normally and the player enters 1B at once. Also assert an outcome earned on the SAME turn the pressure event would fire resolves as the outcome and the scene completes (pin whichever order the engine actually uses; state it in the notes).
(5) Save and load: save mid-scene after the missed window, restore, and assert the same facts, fired events, and that continuing play still behaves as in (3)/(4) with no second firing. Reuse the repo's existing save/restore helpers (grep tests for how other tests snapshot and restore engine state).
(6) A transport retry (the provider raising its transient error, if the stub can) does not advance the window; if the repo has no such error path, skip with a note.
Add (1)-(6) as tests in tests/test_incident_pressure.py. Where today's behavior differs from the expectation, FIRST decide if it violates the contract text above. If yes, fix it with the smallest engine change (under 30 changed lines; scenes without incidents must stay byte-identical in behavior) and say so in the notes; if the fix would be larger, stop, leave the test unmarked-but-failing out of the patch is NOT allowed - instead assert actual behavior, and record exactly what the contract needs. Never use xfail.

KNOWN OPEN QUESTION, do not solve it: after the missed window and with no recovery, nothing ends the scene (no backstop). In the notes write one paragraph saying what a player stuck in that state experiences in the engine today and the smallest design options (for example a recovery storylet declared in the package, or a typed incident field for a withdrawal transition). Do not implement an option.

HOW TO RUN: first confirm PYTHONPATH=$PWD /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -c "import storygame; print(storygame.__file__)" prints a path inside the cwd. Tests: PYTHONPATH=$PWD TMPDIR=/tmp /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider --no-cov tests/test_incident_pressure.py tests/test_incident_engine.py tests/test_incident_loader.py tests/test_incident_characterization.py. Then the FULL suite: PYTHONPATH=$PWD TMPDIR=/tmp /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider --no-cov -n auto (bare pytest, NOT with '.'). Ruff: PYTHONPATH=$PWD /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m ruff check --fix <your files>, then -m ruff format <your files>. Do not run uv. New file under 15 seconds.

NOTES CONTRACT: step4-notes.md: one line per item (1)-(6): what it pins, actual behavior, whether it matched the contract, any engine change with file:line; then the open-question paragraph. Reply with a short summary.
